name: Database
description: A client for PostgreSQL on the desk's own sessions, and MySQL / MariaDB and SQLite through their own command-line clients without a shell: connections, an explorer of every object kind with DDL and row counts, SQL consoles with highlighting, autocomplete, formatting and parameters, results that keep NULL apart with sorting, filtering, paging, a value viewer, a record view, copy and export, pending cell edits applied in one transaction, query plans, history and starred queries, and guards for read-only and production connections.

Database: maintenance (VACUUM, ANALYZE, REINDEX, CLUSTER)
commands.description: Opens the maintenance form of a PostgreSQL table, index, schema or database and answers the statement it runs, in words what it locks and for how long, and the target's size and statistics. With run, it runs the statement alone, outside a transaction block, after the person says yes, and answers how it ended, the server's output and the statistics before and after. A read-only connection refuses.

connection.description: A connection's name or id; the one on screen, or one picked, when absent.

operation.description: What to run; VACUUM by default (REINDEX for an index).

options.description: The statement's options, on the defaults (an open form's own are set aside); what the server's version or another option rules out is left out of the statement.

bufferUsageLimit.description: A size such as 256kB or 16MB, or 0.

using.description: The index CLUSTER orders the table by.

run.description: Run it once the form is open; the person is always asked first.

Database: run a function or procedure
commands.description: Opens the form of a PostgreSQL function or procedure, one field per argument checked by its type, and answers the routine, its arguments with their modes, types and defaults, how it runs (an IMMUTABLE or STABLE function reads; a VOLATILE function or a procedure is a write) and the exact call. With run, it runs the call in the connection's console and answers its rows, the notices and how it ended; a write runs only after the person says yes, a read-only connection refuses one, and rollback runs it in a transaction rolled back at the end.

connection.description: A connection's name or id; the one on screen, or one picked, when absent.

arguments.description: Values by argument name ($1 for one without), or a list in the call's order: null is NULL, a list is a VARIADIC argument's elements, {value, type} gives a polymorphic one its type, and one left out takes its DEFAULT.

rollback.description: Run it in a transaction rolled back at the end (not for a procedure that commits).

run.description: Run the call once the form is open; the person is asked first when it may write.

Database: search the source of routines, views and triggers
commands.description: Looks for a text or a regular expression in the definitions of functions, procedures, views, materialized views, triggers, policies, checks and defaults that the schema cache holds (routine and view bodies read once per read of a schema), in one schema, the connection's database or every connection, and answers each object with its matching lines. Comments too when asked. Without a text it opens the form. It never changes anything.

connection.description: A PostgreSQL connection's name or id; the one on screen, or one picked, when absent.

text.description: What to find; absent or empty opens the form.

regex.description: The text is a regular expression, matched within a line.

comments.description: Search COMMENT ON texts and the comments inside definitions too.

scope.description: One schema (with schema), the connection's database (the default), or every PostgreSQL connection and each cached database of its server.

schema.description: The schema of the scope schema.

kinds.description: The kinds of object to search; all of them when absent.

endue.database.max-rows.description: Rows a result keeps (1 to 100000); More rows loads four times as many.

endue.database.timeout-seconds.description: Stop a run that takes longer, in seconds; 0 waits as long as it takes. PostgreSQL ends the statement on the server (statement_timeout).

endue.database.confirm.description: Ask before statements that change a production connection, and before DROP, TRUNCATE, or UPDATE and DELETE without WHERE anywhere. Agents' writes are always asked.

endue.database.history.description: Keep the statements each connection ran (never their results, never statements that carry a password).

endue.database.history-max.description: How many statements each connection's history keeps (0 to 1000).

endue.database.system-schemas.description: Show the system schemas in the explorer (pg_catalog, information_schema, mysql, sys ...) and PostgreSQL's template databases.

endue.database.mysql.description: The MySQL client: a name on PATH or a full path. Empty: mysql, else mariadb. Any other program or path is asked for at its first run.

endue.database.sqlite3.description: The sqlite3 program: a name on PATH or a full path. Empty: sqlite3. Any other program or path is asked for at its first run.

endue.database.path.description: Folders searched for the clients when they are not on the desk's PATH, before Homebrew's and the system's.

endue.database.format-keyword-case.description: How Format SQL writes PostgreSQL's keywords: upper (SELECT, INT), lower (select, int) or preserve (as typed). Names, strings and quoted identifiers never change.

endue.database.format-indent.description: Spaces a level of PostgreSQL's Format SQL indents (1 to 8).

endue.database.format-line-width.description: The width a line of PostgreSQL's Format SQL keeps to when it can (40 to 240); a longer name or string still goes on one line.

endue.database.format-comma.description: Where a broken list's commas go in PostgreSQL's Format SQL: last (id, then name on the next line) or first (id, then , name).

endue.database.format-and-or.description: Where a broken condition's AND and OR go in PostgreSQL's Format SQL: before (a line starts AND b = 1) or after (a line ends a = 1 AND).

endue.database.format-joins.description: How joins sit in PostgreSQL's Format SQL: flat (JOIN under FROM) or indented (JOIN one level in from FROM).

endue.database.format-one-line.description: What PostgreSQL's Format SQL keeps on one line when it fits: each clause (SELECT a, b then FROM t), the whole statement (SELECT a, b FROM t), or only each item (every list and condition broken one item a line).

endue.database.format-lists.description: Where a broken list goes in PostgreSQL's Format SQL: indent (on the lines under SELECT, one level in) or align (after SELECT, each item under the first).

endue.database.format-on-save.description: Save lays a .sql file's console out with Format SQL before it writes the file, by the format of the file's connection; a file on no connection yet is written as typed.

endue.database.problems-syntax.description: Underline SQL the parser cannot read in PostgreSQL consoles, a pause after typing stops.

endue.database.problems-names.description: Underline tables, columns and schemas that the cached schema does not have, and INSERT column counts that do not match, in PostgreSQL consoles. Nothing is asked of the server.

endue.database.problems-warnings.description: Mark statements that are likely mistakes in PostgreSQL consoles as warnings, each with its identifier and, where the rewrite is certain, a fix. A comment -- endue-ignore <identifiers> turns them off for its line, or for the next line when it stands alone.

endue.database.problems-warnings-off.description: Warnings never marked, by identifier: null-comparison, join-without-condition, select-star, column-cast, not-in-null, update-without-where, delete-without-where, limit-without-order, function-on-indexed-column, insert-without-columns, server-signal, and in PL/pgSQL bodies unused-variable, unreachable-code.

endue.database.pg-dump.description: The pg_dump program: a name on PATH or a full path. Empty: pg_dump. Any other program or path is asked for at its first run.

endue.database.pg-restore.description: The pg_restore program: a name on PATH or a full path. Empty: pg_restore. Any other program or path is asked for at its first run.

endue.database.sessions-per-connection.description: PostgreSQL sessions a connection's consoles and table views keep open at once (1 to 12). At the limit, a table view's idle session closes first; past it, a run says which to close.

endue.database.session-idle-minutes.description: Close a console's or a table view's PostgreSQL session no run used for this many minutes; 0 keeps them open. A session in a transaction is never closed this way.

endue.database.snippets.description: Your own completion snippets: a name (letters, digits and _) to a template, at most 100. ${name} marks a place Tab moves to; the same name is edited together. One named like a built-in snippet (sel, ins, upd, del, upsert, with, ctab, idx, txn, case) replaces it.
